newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cuban foreign minister on discrete Latam journey.
newsitem.headline: Cuban foreign minister on discrete Latam journey.

text.p: Cuban Foreign Minister Robert Robaina made a secret trip to Mexico last week and met with Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, diplomats said on Monday.
The visit to Mexico on Thursday was part of a discrete journey to several Latin American nations, according to sources who spoke on condition of anonymity.
Costa Rican authorities said Robaina would visit their Central American country late Monday, arriving from Panama.
In addition, the Mexican government news agency Notimex said the Cuban foreign minister was in Guatemala on Saturday to meet with President Alvaro Arzu.
The Cuban embassy in Mexico confirmed that Robaina had been in Mexico but refused to answer further questions.
"He passed through Mexico," one embassy source told Reuters, adding that Robaina "will continue his trip" without providing details.
Mexican diplomatic sources told Reuters it was "probable" that Zedillo met with Robaina in the Caribbean resort of Tulum after a meeting there with the leaders of neighboring Honduras and Belize.
But the sources said they did not know if Robaina also met with the Central American leaders in Tulum.
